message.content:
P1 — `NAMED.md` M332 “0x4ddcf1 ... eax is the return of callee 0x5f1394” is not read by `G3`  
`NAMED.md:~1217` (added M332 row 3), gate at `scripts/m332_difficulty_census.py:353-367` and evidence at `evidence/m332_difficulty_census.txt:80`, `:70`  
The VERIFIED claim says 0x4ddcf1’s eax is the return of callee `0x5f1394` on the `jge` edge from `0x4ddb5a`. The gate only proves: the site exists, prior parsed insn is `ret`, one branch target is `0x4ddb5a`, `0x4ddb5a` mnemonic is `jge`, and the address appears zero times as a raw LE dword. It never inspects `eax`, never finds `call 0x5f1394` on that edge, and never proves `eax` survives between the call and the store. No listed mutant (`MU1-3,8,16`) can redden the “callee 0x5f1394 / return value” part, because the instrument does not measure it. This is exactly a gate that stays green while the claimed def/origin fact is false.

P1 — M332’s “no undisguised writer exists / who writes it is decidable” is overclaimed by the encoding cross-check  
`NAMED.md:~1215` (row 1), `scripts/m332_difficulty_census.py:184-197`, `scripts/m332_difficulty_census.py:203-219`  
`G1` compares the objdump text-reference set with a raw byte-substring scan over each parsed instruction’s bytes and asserts `len(matrefs) == 0`. That only shows those two scans currently agree on `.text` cache lines. It does not prove there is no indirect writer: an indexed/base-register store with a computed address, a `lea`/`add` cursor followed by `[reg]` store, or another memory form that objdump may not print as `ds:0x985aec` is invisible if it has no immediate bytes equal to the target. The evidence line says “0 address materializations” and “set-identical”, but the prose turns that into “no undisguised writer exists”. A real writer could be outside the scanned forms and none of the mutants can redden the claim about all possible writers.

P1 — `0x57c7b5` “co-store of the same eax ... no intervening write” is not verified by the M332 clean-copy gate  
`NAMED.md:~1008` modified M308 row, and `scripts/m332_difficulty_census.py:253-289`, evidence `:14-18`  
The M308 row still carries a VERIFIED provenance claim: `0x57c7b5` is a co-store of the same eax as `0x57c7b0`, no intervening write. M332’s `G4` records a copy pair only by load-site and store-site with register liveness, e.g. `(0x92bde8, 0x92bde8?)` / sites. It does not verify that the value stored at `0x57c7b0` and `0x57c7b5` is the same register value, nor that no intervening instruction writes either source or register. `MU2` only nops one store and reddens G1-G4 structurally; it does not test co-store semantics. Therefore the cited gate reads addresses and a crude liveness pattern, not the claimed “same eax / no intervening write” law.

P2 — The pref table claims to have identified `GetPrivateProfileStringA` / `WritePrivateProfileStringA`, but the instrument classifies only by push-run arity  
`NAMED.md:~1219`, `scripts/m332_difficulty_census.py:310-331`, evidence `:33-36`, `:66`  
Claims: “each 6-arg `GetPrivateProfileStringA` push window” and “its 8 four-arg pushes == the 8 `WritePrivateProfileStringA` Ghidra resolves there”. Code selects READ by `argc == 6`, WRITE by `argc == 4`, and counts name pushes near calls. It never resolves the call target, import ordinal, PLT, string, or Ghidra function name for those calls. A four- or six-argument call to another API would still be counted. The fact that the pairing is interesting does not make the API identity VERIFIED; the named mutants can move name/field rows but cannot make an `argc==4` detector distinguish `WritePrivateProfileStringA` from an unrelated four-arg callee.

P2 — The Ghidra “third independent view” is not independent in the claimed per-call sense  
`scripts/m332_difficulty_census.py:365-386`, evidence `:48-64`, NAMED row `:1219`  
`G7` requires three-way agreement on 6 names and sibling fields. The decompiler parser scans the bodies of `FUN_0058e7f0` and `FUN_0058f0d0`, sets `pend = name` whenever a `s_Name_...` string appears, then attaches every later `DAT_xxx=` assignment to that same `pend` until another name appears. It never resets after an assignment, never anchors to the profile call’s return/value, and merges both functions into one dictionary. The claim says the pseudocode “pairs it a third way,” which implies assignment/call association; the gate merely reproduces a name-to-DAT set that its own unanchored scanner creates.

P2 — Clean-copy sites are pinned, but “no intervening write” for the copied memory cell is not enforced  
`scripts/m332_difficulty_census.py:253-289`, evidence `:11-18`  
The copy law says: load a cell into a register, then store that register to another cell, with no intervening clobber. Code kills register provenance on register redefinition and calls, but it does not kill or inspect writes to the source cell itself. For a pair like `0x92bde8 -> 0x985aec`, if the source cell were stored between the load and the store, the reported relation could be false, yet `COPY_SITES` and `G4` would still pass because the exact load/store addresses remain present. This weakens the measured DEFINITION behind “clean-copy map” and especially the master→runtime mirror claim.

P2 — M332’s “cmp immediates exactly {1,2,3,4}” is gated only on the immediate subset; the register compare is not pinned  
`NAMED.md:~1215`, `scripts/m332_difficulty_census.py:220-223`, `scripts/m332_difficulty_census.py:475-480`, evidence `:5`  
The prose says the cmp operands are exactly `{1,2,3,4}` “+1 vs ebx”. The gate checks that the subset of cmp operands matching `IMM` is exactly `{"0x1","0x2","0x3","0x4"}`. It does not require the non-immediate cmp operand set to be `{"ebx"}` or even that any register compare exists. If an additional non-immediate compare operand were present, or the ebx arm were removed, G1 could remain green on the immediate law. The `ebx` part of the printed measurement is not pinned as a verified fact.

P2 — The array-end “RIVAL KILLED” row only proves a backward immediate walk, not a real array-bound loop  
`NAMED.md:~1221`, `scripts/m332_difficulty_census.py:418-447`, evidence `:70-74`  
The claim says `0x92bde8` is the exact end of a 4x0xd4 record array with loop-bound uses. `G8` confirms two `cmp ... ,0x92bde8` immediates and then walks backward for a register-setting `add/sub imm` and `mov imm`. It does not verify the loop’s conditional jump, the loop body, or that `0x92ba98` really indexes a 0xd4-stride array. The scalar-store/load part is good, but the array-end characterization rests on a heuristic immediate walk that is gated only to reproduce this shape. A false “array end” interpretation could still pass if the immediate pattern exists.

P2 — `scripts/m332_named_rotate.py` is non-idempotent and not byte-exact about the stub actually left behind  
`scripts/m332_named_rotate.py:65-70`, `:56-62`; `NAMED.md:215-219`  
The script asserts the archive contains the moved block, then writes a replacement stub. It only asserts the first stub line is present and the old `START` heading is not in the prefix. It does not assert the full stub text, and the final `NAMED.md` stub differs from the `STUB` constant embedded in the script (for example “harness era starts at `## M308`” vs “harness era begins at `## M308`”, shorter bullets, evidence placement). The rotation claim “EVERY address and gate body VERBATIM ... this stub governs” is partly a docs-only prose claim; at minimum, the rotation tool does not prove the hot-file stub is the one it intends to install. Also, because it refuses if the archive exists, the PR cannot be safely replayed after the file has been created without manual surgery.

P2 — The harness selftest’s “exactly one declared NO-OP” is weaker than it reads  
`scripts/m332_mutate.py:92-105`, evidence `:16-19`  
`ST4` requires `noops == ["MU16"]`, which is fine for declared no-ops. But the final harness success only requires each mutant’s observed red set to equal its declared set. `MU16` is declared `set()`, and evidence shows it reddens `[]`. However, a mutant that reddens nothing because it targets a site that is not read by any gate is indistinguishable from a declared NO-OP. The harness measures declared-vs-observed agreement, not “this mutant touches a measured literal/instruction consumed by a gate.” This is acceptable for explicitly declared NO-OPs, but the repo law says every VERIFIED row must name a mutant that reddens the claim; rows whose claim includes unmeasured origin/API/decompiler facts can pass on adjacent structural redness only.
